races.name: Darlington Ra & Ellie Wake Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley runner freshened off a 7-day gap, winning form at 16f on Good is directly relevant, but this is a genuine hold-up horse who will find himself racing mid-pack rather than from the rear he prefers — the style mismatch tempers what his OR of 120 and recent 1-2 form suggest on paper.

runners_data.name: Cadillac Ranch
runners_data.note: Extraordinarily light form profile — one run in Goodish ground showing a win, then a string of pull-ups — makes this runner deeply opaque; Miss Callwood claims 7lbs and LJ Morgan has a quiet 14-day strike rate, so treat with caution regardless of price.

runners_data.name: Credit Union
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures of 0000 across soft and Good ground at trips from 17-20f point firmly toward a horse that finishes well down the field; the hood is noted but has not sparked any improvement to date, and the hold-up style is further compromised by redistribution into a crowded mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Rock Armour
runners_data.note: A 95-day break is a significant flag here — David Thompson's yard has a modest 14-day return rate — and the flat form base (placed in Good-ground sprints) suggests stamina for 2m4f is unproven; naturally a hold-up type but will be racing in a compressed midfield pack.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Two consecutive sixth-place efforts over 2m (Good) suggest the horse is running consistently but not threatening to win; Ryan Mania's booking is the positive angle, though the hold-up profile and unremarkable TS figures make this an each-way outsider at best.

runners_data.name: Datstheholyallofit
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race and the key pace-shape horse — Brian Hughes, Sedgefield's premier jockey, takes over and the horse arrives off a 9-day turnaround having won at 16f Good last time; T14 of 2/7 for Neville is respectable, and Good ground across all four recent runs gives strong confidence in the going.

runners_data.name: Orestina
runners_data.note: Won over a similar distance at Huntingdon on Standard ground and has winning form, but the hood and a 44-day gap are both worth noting; Rebecca Menzies has a moderate 1/14 T14 return, and this natural hold-up type is squeezed into a midfield role that dilutes the impact of what is otherwise an interesting form angle.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby's 4yo is lightly raced over hurdles and best flat form came at shorter trips (8-10f), so the 2m4f trip represents a significant stamina question; Charlie Maggs claims 3lbs, the hood is first-time, and the hold-up style means she needs a lot to go right in a bunched field.

races.paceDynamic: Datstheholyallofit is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Brian Hughes aboard and four recent runs all over similar Good ground at similar trips, he is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control tempo entirely on his own terms. With no horse in this field possessing both the inclination and the form to challenge him for the lead, the pace will be honest but not pressurising — a rhythm that suits a relaxed gallop through the early stages of this 2m4f trip. The field behind him is composed almost entirely of hold-up types — Genealogy, Credit Union, Rock Armour, Orestina, and others — who will be queuing up in the pack with nowhere to go, unable to express their natural style. This race shape heavily favours a horse who can travel prominently behind the leader or, ideally, Datstheholyallofit himself if he sustains his gallop to the last — the bunched hold-up brigade will face a tactical traffic problem and a finishing burst from a lone leader who has had it easy in front. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically race at the rear in isolation; Genealogy and Orestina are most likely to be pushed forward out of role, but Rock Armour and Credit Union will also be crowded into an uncharacteristic mid-pack position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Datstheholyallofit Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Datstheholyallofit is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and lands running at the last.
scenarios.body: Hughes settles him into a controlled but confidence-boosting lead and the horse, who won over C&D-equivalent and has form figures of 44-12 improving sharply, simply outstays the backmarkers who cannot close from the pack in time. The lone-leader shape is the most probable outcome given the absence of any other natural front-runner, and Good ground suits his record.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse — most likely Genealogy or Orestina — travels prominently out of role and swoops before the last.
scenarios.body: Genealogy has the highest OR and recent winning form, and if she (or a similarly redistributed runner) manages to sit just off the leader and tracks Datstheholyallofit through the race, she could produce a late burst to nail him close home. This is plausible but discounted because Genealogy is a true hold-up type racing out of role, making it harder to deliver a clean, well-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Datstheholyallofit ties up badly from two out, opening a gap for a closer to rattle home.
scenarios.body: In this scenario a genuinely held-up runner — Sweet Cicely or Tracker Issue — finds a gap late and finishes best of all, but this requires a pace scenario that the current map does not strongly support given the sustainable tempo expected. Sweet Cicely's last run showed a placed effort over this sort of trip, but the style and redistribution context make this a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded midfield creates interference, fallers, or significant traffic issues that reshuffle the race order dramatically.
scenarios.body: Rock Armour, returning from 95 days off and with flat-form that shows placed efforts at sprint trips, could benefit if the pack bunches tightly and chaos opens a gap; Cadillac Ranch's unknown form profile (1PPP-P) is a wildcard who could outrun a big price if the race falls apart. This is the least likely shape but exists as a genuine risk given eight runners with compressed styles.

watchPoints.text: Datstheholyallofit — if Brian Hughes is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the outset, monitor whether the leader's lead extends or is pegged back from the third-last, as that will define whether the scenario closes or opens.

Genealogy — watch the early stages to see whether Harry Kimber elects to push forward out of natural hold-up role to sit closer to Datstheholyallofit; if he does, this runner becomes significantly more dangerous than the map alone suggests.

Cadillac Ranch — the string of pull-ups after a win is a genuine welfare and safety concern in a jumping race; watch for any early signs of reluctance or jumping errors from this deeply unexposed runner.

Rock Armour — returning from 95 days off with a flat-form base and an unproven stamina profile; if the horse travels sweetly in the early stages this absence concern diminishes, but watch for signs of laboured jumping beyond 2m.

Sweet Cicely — first-time hood combined with an unproven stamina trip could produce an erratic early-race display; the horse's behaviour at the start and over the first two flights will indicate whether the headgear has had a calming or unsettling effect.

races.name: Newts Rocket To The Top Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Daaris
runners_data.note: Consistent hurdler with solid recent form (3-3-3-4) and positive course-and-distance experience at Sedgefield; hold-up style suits a race where a late challenge is feasible if the pace builds, and 38 days since last run for Kevin & Lauren Frost appears straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Daaris has been knocking persistently on the door, placing third in three of his last five starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions with our rating putting him narrowly top of this field; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must finally convert.

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's five-year-old was second on good ground 13 days ago and brings strong recent form; a natural hold-up horse who has placed ten times in fifteen starts on similar going, though will need to be closer to the pace than usual given the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistent profile and has run over today's trip and going before, with a second in recent starts giving him solid claims here; the main risk is he remains winless in his last five and may again find one too good.

runners_data.name: Expert Analysis
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fade flag and a concerning recent form string (C580-P) with no wins or places on good ground in nine starts; 94 days off the track for Jennie Candlish is a notable absence, and the horse's tendency to weaken late makes this compressed, slow-run shape an uncomfortable fit.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Expert Analysis does at least return with distance and going experience to call upon, though 94 days off the track and a taxing 164 lb burden make confidence hard to sustain.

runners_data.name: Hijo de La Luna
runners_data.note: Showed some form with a third last time out in good ground conditions, but wears a visor and is a genuine hold-up operator who will struggle to express his natural style in a field this rear-heavy; Bruce Lynn faces a tactical puzzle getting him into play from an awkward position.
runners_data.comment: Hijo de La Luna brings experience over today's trip and going, and a third three starts back hints at ability, though he remains winless in recent starts; fit off a 13-day break and carrying 160 lb, our rating of 92 makes him an interesting proposition at a mark of 88.

runners_data.name: Return With Gold
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter — Brian Hughes can control this race from the front under a light weight of 154lbs, and three recent starts at OR 85 show he is competitive on good ground; the solo front-running role is a clear opportunity but his modest form figures (3-4-) remind us he has yet to win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Return With Gold faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back offers slim encouragement, but 154 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at OR 79 who has been placed four times in fourteen good-ground starts, but all five recent runs have come over 18f-24f — this 2m1f trip looks short of his best, and his true hold-up style is squeezed further into midfield by redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yanka Blue has shown consistent placing ability — second last time out and second two starts back — though weight at 151 lb may test her, and she drops away sharply in the formbook beyond that promising recent pair.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Has a recent second on good ground to his name but carries a ⚠ fade flag alongside a visor, and his true racing style is closer to the rear than midfield; the shorter 2m1f trip may not play to his strengths given five runs at longer distances recently.
runners_data.comment: Littletown Lad has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with promise when second last time out, though that unseating two starts back clouds his profile; winless in his last five starts and carrying 151 lb, he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: Modest form figures (50-086) with no wins or places across eight good-ground starts, and the ⚠ fade flag compounds concern; bumped forward on the map from his natural hold-up berth, making his realistic chance in this shape thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Breaking Ground faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and the 57-day break at least means she arrives fresh, though recent form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied and placed once in fifteen good-ground starts, with a recent pulled-up on his card; a genuine closer who is mapped ahead of his natural position, and Charlie Maggs' 3lb claim helps on weight but the form profile offers limited encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up on one of those occasions, Red Trail is hard to fancy from her recent profile, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Scopic
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 59 with headgear (hood and tongue-tie) and no wins or places across four good-ground starts; a natural hold-up type displaced further forward on the map, and the ratings gap alone makes this a very tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement despite being yet to win in his last four starts, Scopic returns after 39 days carrying 145 lb, and with limited form to go on, there remains plenty to find out about this gelding.

races.paceDynamic: Return With Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no significant pace pressure emerging from elsewhere, Brian Hughes should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 2m1f trip on good ground at Sedgefield. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Hijo de La Luna, Yanka Blue, Littletown Lad, Breaking Ground, Red Trail and Scopic are all genuine closers who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because there is no room for them all at the rear; in reality, most will race further back than their mapped positions suggest. With one horse controlling a measured pace and a wall of hold-up horses behind needing a strong gallop to generate momentum, the race shape is likely to compress into a bunched approach to the home straight, where the ability to travel smoothly close to the pace becomes the decisive asset. This race shape firmly favours a horse that can sit just off Return With Gold — in second or third — without expending energy, travel fluently over these hurdles and simply pick up when the pace drops away; prominent racers who secure an early advantageous position are best placed, while true closers needing a searching gallop to close on face an awkward setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Return With Gold Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Return With Gold is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a comfortable clip and the hold-up pack cannot generate sufficient momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: Return With Gold sets an unchallenged, well-judged pace under Brian Hughes and simply keeps finding on the run-in before rivals can close the gap; horses who sit prominently in second or third benefit most as they track the leader without effort and challenge on level terms at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Patient Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and one of the better-class hold-up horses finds their natural position and delivers a clean late run.
scenarios.body: A runner like Daaris or Character Testing, tracking midfield and travelling well, produces a smooth run up the inner on the home turn and hits the front approaching the last when Return With Gold's lead begins to fade; on good ground at Sedgefield the trip suits an efficient jumper who can quicken off a steady clip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Return With Gold's rider judges the pace perfectly, jumping slickly, and the chasing pack simply has too much ground to make up from the rear.
scenarios.body: Return With Gold extends clear after the second-last with rivals still shuffling for position behind, the compressed, slow-run nature of the race leaving hold-up horses with no room to launch a proper challenge; a wire-to-wire success becomes achievable at a competitive handicap mark of OR 85.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes a mass surge turning for home with multiple hold-up horses arriving simultaneously, creating a chaotic finish where the best-handicapped horse prevails.
scenarios.body: The compressed race shape produces a sprint finish over the final two hurdles with little between several runners, favouring the horse with the most residual class or a well-drawn position on the rail; redistributed types who manage to secure a better position than expected earlier could be involved.

watchPoints.text: Return With Gold is the only confirmed pace-setter — if Brian Hughes misses the break or is forced wider than expected in the early stages, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses gain a significant advantage.

Hijo de La Luna, Yanka Blue, Littletown Lad, Breaking Ground, Red Trail and Scopic are all genuine closers crammed into midfield on the map — watch for interference and crowding on the first circuit as these horses scramble for realistic positions.

Yanka Blue's recent runs have all been over 18f to 24f; the drop to 2m1f is a significant trip reduction and her finishing effort could come too late if she fails to adapt her hold-up style to a shorter, faster race.

Expert Analysis has been off the track 94 days and shows a ⚠ fade flag with no good-ground form working in her favour — monitor in the market; if she drifts sharply pre-race, the absence and stamina concerns may be more significant than the OR 95 rating implies.

Character Testing ran just 13 days ago and is the most recently raced hold-up horse with a genuine place chance — watch how quickly she settles and whether Jamie Hamilton elects to track Return With Gold closely rather than risk being swallowed up in the hold-up pack.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Delpotro
runners_data.note: Front-runner with solid Good-ground form (12/15, 2 wins, 7 places) but faces stiff early competition for the lead from Fiskardo and Tom Creen; 59 days off and tongue-tie in use, trainer Longsdon has a cold strike rate (0/3 last 14 days).|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Delpotro has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 108 marks him out as a leading danger at the weights; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts and a 59-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with a clean Good-ground record — every recent run on this surface has produced a placing — and Jennie Candlish's yard is 2/10 in the past fortnight, giving this one a live each-way profile; 43 days since last run is straightforward.|
runners_data.comment: Thank You Blue arrives winless in his last five starts but has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; at 165 lb he faces a stiff ask, but our rating of 115 marks him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Fiskardo
runners_data.note: In-form six-year-old, fit from a run just nine days ago, with Mickey Bowen's yard firing at 3/14 recently; front-runner whose Good-ground record (5/7, 1W 3P) is the most concentrated pace-map fit in the race and Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim is a weight bonus.|
runners_data.comment: Fiskardo showed a tidy mix of consistency and ability when winning and finishing second and third in recent starts, and he returns on a quick nine-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before; the burden of 165 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Wherearethejudges
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who arrives 193 days off the track — freshness is either an asset or a concern; all recent form on Soft, so today's Good ground is an unknown quantity, and the limited form string makes reading his current level difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up most recently, Wherearethejudges carries 163 lb on his return from 193 days off, which is the key question here; he has run over today's trip before, but a rating of 96 ranking him sixth of nine underlines the size of the task.

runners_data.name: Wudya
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with an outstanding record on Good ground (13/15 sim-going runs, 2W 5P) and the blinkers plus tongue-tie combination suggests connections are asking for more; 35 days off is fine, though the trainer partnership is 0/1 recently.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Wudya nonetheless shaped with promise when fourth two runs back and again three runs back, and has run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is a hefty 163 lb on her back.

runners_data.name: Tom Creen
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old front-runner returning from a 140-day absence — he is the most vulnerable of the three pace-setters for freshness and race-sharpness; limited wins on Good ground (0W 4P from 7 runs) and Jonathan England's mount has pulled up or unseated in recent starts.|
runners_data.comment: Tom Creen has experience over today's trip and going, and his third two starts back offers some encouragement, but he is winless in his last five starts, returns after 140 days off, and unseated last time out — all giving pause on his claims from stall.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with exceptional Good-ground reliability (14/15 runs on similar going, 1W 6P) and Philip Kirby's yard is 3/13 in the past fortnight; only 13 days since his last run keeps him race-sharp, though he operates from the widest weights range and must navigate expected traffic.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Clean Getaway faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before and comes back quickly after 13 days, and he carries 149 lb.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose headgear (visor) denotes a horse that needs to be kept interested; Good-ground record is moderate (7/15, 1W 3P) and Mark Walford's yard is a cold 0/9 in the past 14 days — 41 days off is straightforward but trainer form is a flag.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Huit Reflets faces a stiff ask at 149 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going and does show some consistency, finishing second twice in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Prominent-style nine-year-old whose 15/15 runs have come on similar going but without a win (0W 3P) — consistency without a killer punch; trainer Barry John Murphy is 0/3 recently and recent form shows a pull-up last time, making confidence hard to build.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Applejack Poet's case is not helped by a pulled-up effort last time, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 40-day break carrying 146 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Delpotro, Fiskardo, and Tom Creen all want to lead, making a strong, sustained gallop from the off almost certain at Sedgefield over this 2m3½f trip on Good ground. The field holds more front-running types than can all get their position simultaneously — Fiskardo, fresh off a run nine days ago and trained by an in-form Mickey Bowen yard, looks best-placed to actually secure the rail, with Delpotro likely to dispute and Tom Creen — an 11-year-old off a 140-day absence — the most likely to concede ground early. Four runners want a prominent pitch (Thank You Blue, Wudya, Huit Reflets, Applejack Poet) creating a congested pack 2-3 out where interference is a genuine risk, particularly approaching the final fences. This race shape — a genuine, unrelenting pace over an honest distance — heavily favours the confirmed hold-up or midfield horses who carry natural stamina reserves and can deliver a clean late run when the front-runners crack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle between Delpotro, Fiskardo, and Tom Creen burns each other out before the final circuit, the hold-up and midfield horses come into their own off a scorching fractions-set tempo. Wherearethejudges and Clean Getaway, both genuine hold-up types, can arrive late on a proper gallop that strips the front-runners of any residual kick at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fiskardo Controls Front
scenarios.trigger: If Fiskardo secures a clear lead and settles into a rhythm, using his recent race fitness (9 days ago) to dictate an honest but not suicidal pace, he has the stamina profile to hold on. His Good-ground form reads consistently (5/7 runners in similar going) and jockey Shane Fenelon can afford to conserve enough to repel late challenges, particularly from the prominent-style rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures early and one of the prominent-style horses (Thank You Blue or Wudya) slots just off the leaders without over-committing, they strike a balance between tracking the pace and arriving fresh at the final two fences. Thank You Blue has the strongest Good-ground prominent record in the field and Jennie Candlish's yard is 2/10 in the past fortnight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Race, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the midfield pack between 2-3 out — a real risk given the prominent congestion — a more experienced or lower-weighted finisher picks through the carnage. Clean Getaway's consistency over Good ground (14/15 runs) and Philip Kirby's 3/13 recent yard form make him the most likely beneficiary of a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Thank You Blue, Wudya, Huit Reflets, and Applejack Poet all want the same patch of ground 2-3 out; watch for interference, checked runs, or jumping errors in this group that could end winning chances in a moment.

Tom Creen is a front-runner returning 140 days fresh with recent pull-up and unseating entries in his form; if he flukes the lead and then fades sharply, he is a serious falling risk that could take out other runners.

Fiskardo ran just nine days ago — watch for signs of fatigue or a flat jump in the back straight; if he is clearly flat by the 12th fence, the race becomes genuinely open and the closers benefit sharply.

Wherearethejudges has been off 193 days and all his recent form came on Soft — watch his jumping sharpness on Good ground in the early stages; a mistake at an early fence after a long absence could see Callum Bewley quickly out of the race.

Delpotro's trainer Charlie Longsdon is 0/3 in the past 14 days — worth noting whether Sean Bowen rides him vigorously for the lead or settles back slightly, which would be a significant pace-map signal for the race as a whole.

races.name: Warm-Flo Hot To Trot Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: Won twice at 2m (16f) on Good in his last four outings and comes here fresh at 44 days off for Jamie Snowden — a handler who fires horses fit enough to front-run; sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, which hands him total race control.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in good heart, Machete Beach has won twice in his last five starts with a second last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the 44-day break is the one query, but his rating of 120 makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old carrying headgear (tongue-strap/t-piece) who goes well on Good (10/15 sim-going, 2W) but has been out of form lately (7-4-1-7 in recent runs); Miss Rebecca Hitchen claims 10lb which helps on OR, but his natural hold-up style is genuinely suited to the rear and he needs the pace to lift.
runners_data.comment: Glory And Honour landed a win three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating of 120 marking him as a leading threat — the concern is a seventh last time out that he must put behind him here.

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Back from 66 days off for Jennie Candlish, who strikes at 2/10 in the last 14 days — form figures show back-to-back wins (1-1) in his most recent starts, both on Good, and the trip (17-18f range) is right in his wheelhouse; a genuine hold-up horse who will appreciate any pace injection.
runners_data.comment: Saint Polo arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, making him a serious threat at the head of the market; the main concern is a 66-day absence since that last success.

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's seven-year-old has a win on Good at this trip (1/17f/GOO) and returns 41 days fresh; a true hold-up horse by nature, but in a six-runner race he will be compressed closer to the pace than he wants, which tempers confidence in him producing his best late run.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner five starts back, Jolie Coeur Allen brings distance and going experience alongside a rating of 107 to make her a genuine threat here; the main concern is the 41-day absence.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight on Good going (3W/8P sim-going) and took a U in his most recent run; another genuine hold-up type who, in a small-field tactical race, will struggle to secure his preferred rearward position — the redistribution reflects real race-shape pressure rather than a stylistic choice.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures and carrying a hefty 158 lb, Scots Poet is hard to fancy at the weights, and an unseated rider last time out does nothing to boost confidence, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Just 13 days since his last run, racing for Adam Nicol (0/5 T14), and his most recent form shows a fall (U) alongside a win — a prominent racer who will likely fill the second slot behind Machete Beach; 97 OR gives him weight relief but his jumping consistency in this company is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Fine Point unseated last time out and ranks last on our figures in a six-runner field, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Machete Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to push him from the front, will dictate at whatever tempo suits Gavin Sheehan and Jamie Snowden's gameplan over this 2m1f trip on Good ground at Sedgefield. Fine Point is the only other horse likely to race prominently, and while he will sit close behind, he lacks the natural gate-speed to threaten Machete Beach's lead — meaning the pace is controlled, sustainable, and unlikely to stretch the field excessively. Glory And Honour, Saint Polo, Jolie Coeur Allen, and Scots Poet all want to race from further back, but this field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Jolie Coeur Allen and Scots Poet, both redistributed in the mapping, are the most likely to find themselves racing closer than ideal, simply because there is nowhere else to go in a six-runner field. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a measured, uncontested pace on Good turf — strongly favours the prominent-to-front profile that can control fractions and simply outstay any late challenge, with genuine closers handicapped by a lack of the sustained gallop they need to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Machete Beach Leads Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and the closers never generate sufficient momentum to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Sheehan settles Machete Beach comfortably in front, the Good ground suits his profile (sim-going 6/9, 3W), and the lack of any pace rival means he is never asked a hard question until the final climb. Fine Point, tracking in second, is the obvious danger but has shown vulnerability (U in recent form) and lacks the OR edge to collar a horse coasting on his own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Out
scenarios.trigger: If Fine Point applies enough pressure to soften Machete Beach and both finish clear of the hold-up horses who fail to close.
scenarios.body: A two-horse war develops between the front pair from the penultimate flight, with the holding ground at Sedgefield rewarding horses who stay handy rather than those making late runs from off the pace. The hold-up horses, compressed into a bunch midfield, never get a clear run at the leaders in a small field with controlled fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach sets a genuinely strong early gallop that burns him out before the last, leaving a closing gap for a fresh hold-up performer.
scenarios.body: Saint Polo and Glory And Honour carry solid Going form (sim-going profiles) and would benefit if the pace uncharacteristically lifts and the leaders come back to them from two out. However, this scenario partly depends on Jolie Coeur Allen and Scots Poet — both redistributed from their natural hold-up position — actually racing in their preferred style, which is less likely in a six-runner field with limited cover.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach is headed or makes a costly jumping error, scrambling the race shape and producing an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: A stumble at a flight or an uncharacteristic exit from his comfort zone forces Sheehan to make hard decisions, bunching the field and creating a messy sprint to the line where the freshest horse (Fine Point, just 13 days since last run) or one of the hold-up types catches a lucky bounce. This is the lowest-probability shape because Machete Beach has shown consistent jumping form and solid handler confidence.

watchPoints.text: Machete Beach is the only horse who sets the pace — if Gavin Sheehan is uncharacteristically aggressive at the start and goes too fast, the whole race shape collapses and the hold-up horses come into play.
Fine Point ran just 13 days ago and has a recent unseating on his card — watch for any jumping hesitancy early that could destabilise his prominent position and expose him to the leaders.
Jolie Coeur Allen and Scots Poet are both genuine hold-up horses squeezed into a small field; if they jostle for cover behind the front pair, interference between them at a flight is a real risk.

Saint Polo returns from 66 days off — Jennie Candlish is in modest 14-day form (2/10) but his back-to-back wins make him the most interesting hold-up threat if the pace is even marginally stronger than expected in the final half-mile.

Glory And Honour is a ten-year-old with a bumpy recent form string; the 10lb claim from Miss Hitchen is worth watching as it could make his OR look attractively lenient if he recaptures the form that earned his two Good-ground wins.

races.name: Bodhi Bespoke Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Getaway Vic
runners_data.note: Strong course and going form (2W6P at sim going, 7/7 record in Good ground), races prominently by nature and gets to lead unchallenged here; the STYLE_FIT flag is largely irrelevant as the race map has it correctly placed at the head of affairs — the 49-day break is the only mild query.
runners_data.comment: Getaway Vic has been placing consistently, finishing second two starts back and second three starts back, and his experience on today's going is a clear asset; the main concern is a 49-day absence that leaves his current sharpness an open question.

runners_data.name: Maggies Boy
runners_data.note: Won last time (2/24f/GOO) and has course experience under Quinlan, but a natural hold-up profile means he requires a genuine test of stamina to land his strong run; the 57-day absence and a pull-up in his form string add mild fitness questions over this extended trip.
runners_data.comment: Maggies Boy shaped well when second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with that experience counting in his favour here; the 57-day absence is the one query, but he carries 161 lb off a mark of 98 with plenty to recommend him.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: Consistent form string (3W7P at sim going) and a recent win over 26f makes the trip credible; races prominently and is one of two horses likely to push Getaway Vic hardest — trainer Sam England has been quiet (0/4 in 14 days) but Jeteye's own profile gives it solid place claims regardless.
runners_data.comment: Jeteye returns off a 41-day break having won last time out, with two victories in his last five starts and experience of today's going working in his favour; the main concern is whether the 158 lb burden blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Consistent in Good-ground handicaps but OR 83 and a hold-up style mean he faces an uphill task against a front-runner setting a sensible tempo; best Going form is Soft (1W1P) so the firm-ish Good surface is a mild concern, and the 41-day absence is neutral.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two starts back and unplaced the run before that make him hard to recommend, and our rating of 82 ranks him sixth of seven here; he has run over today's going before and returns after 41 days, but the recent profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Uncle Al
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose true running style sits behind even the midfield map position he's been allocated — effectively a rear-of-field mover in reality — which materially discounts his chance in a race where the pace is steady and the lead horse is well within himself; a 13-day turnaround and an OR of 82 limit upside.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Uncle Al has shown he can find the frame but a pulled up and an unseated flank that sequence; ranked last of seven on our figures, he looks hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Jo Arengeot Bey AA
runners_data.note: Won 24f on Good under similar conditions and races prominently, so he should naturally find a position just behind Getaway Vic; trainer McCain is cold (0/6 in 14 days) but Sheehan is an experienced jumps handler and the horse's recent second keeps form live.
runners_data.comment: Jo Arengeot Bey AA arrives on the back of a second last time out and a win three starts back, showing he retains ability on his favoured going; the main risk is that pull-up two starts back, which must give some pause.

runners_data.name: Croagh Patrick
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 who has placed at 24f Good but hasn't won in five starts and is a true hold-up type mapped forward due to redistribution — the actual race pattern will see him hunting from the rear; Boanas has no 14-day runners and the 61-day break over an extended trip is a stamina/fitness risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up on his most recent outing 61 days ago, Croagh Patrick faces a stiff task off 142 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and that second two starts back offers some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Getaway Vic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner chase over 3m2½f, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, James Bowen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a luxury that strongly suits a horse with a 2W6P record at this trip and going combination. Jeteye and Jo Arengeot Bey AA will press prominently behind, creating a small lead group but no meaningful pace battle to unsettle Getaway Vic's rhythm. The hold-up horses — Maggies Boy, You Did, Uncle Al, and Croagh Patrick — will need a strong late injection of pace to reel in a front-runner who has not been pressured into going too fast; at 3m2½f on Good ground with a modest, steady tempo, that late run is far from guaranteed. This race shape emphatically favours prominent and front-running profiles; hold-up horses are asked to close ground that may never appear. Note that Uncle Al and Croagh Patrick are true hold-up types compressed into midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up runners than genuine rear-of-field slots — both are unlikely to race as forward as their mapped position suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Getaway Vic Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway Vic is allowed to bowl along at a measured pace and none of the prominent rivals press hard enough to force a genuine test.
scenarios.body: Bowen settles Getaway Vic in front, the pace is fair but never gruelling, and the 3m2½f trip plays to the horse's stamina and jumping rhythm; the hold-up horses close but find Getaway Vic has too much in reserve at the last fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Make It Competitive
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye and Jo Arengeot Bey AA push forward assertively and force a stronger-than-expected pace, unsettling Getaway Vic's economy.
scenarios.body: A truer gallop over the marathon trip stretches the field and places a premium on jumping accuracy and stamina, where Jeteye's recent winning form at this sort of distance holds appeal; Jo Arengeot Bey AA's second last time out shows it handles honest pace well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a jumping error disrupts the leaders in the final circuit, opening the door for a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: Maggies Boy, a course winner on Good ground with a strong late profile under Quinlan, is best placed to exploit any carnage in front, but the scenario requires the race to go wrong for the leaders — a low-probability event.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chase, Survivor Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of the long trip, jumping errors, or a deteriorating pace sees multiple market principles fall away late.
scenarios.body: With several older horses carrying significant weight over 3m2½f, a war of attrition could play into the hands of whichever horse avoids mishap late; Croagh Patrick has course form and may stay on past weakened rivals, though age and recent form are concerns.

watchPoints.text: Getaway Vic's jumping — if Bowen gets in a tangle at any fence in the final mile, Jeteye is immediately on terms and the whole shape flips in favour of the prominent runners.
Jeteye's rider Jonathan England will decide how aggressively to press for second early; if he commits hard to push Getaway Vic, the pace lifts and the hold-up horses' chances improve markedly.
Maggies Boy's ability to land a blow from the rear depends entirely on Quinlan judging a perfectly timed move from the home turn — in a slowly-run race of this length, the window could be narrow.

Uncle Al's 13-day turnaround is the shortest in the field; watch the market for any sign of market support that might indicate trainer confidence in freshness, which would be the key condition for this horse to run to its best.

Going described as Good throughout the card — no significant deterioration reported — which consistently supports front-runners and prominent racers at Sedgefield and reinforces the dominant scenario.

races.name: MW Civils & Groundworks Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with solid good-going form at 2m and 2m2f; Sean Quinlan a key booking for Jennie Candlish who fires at 52-day absences, but the step up to 2m4f is an untested stamina question at OR 96.
runners_data.comment: Aimeric has been knocking on the door with three consecutive fourths in recent starts, and his experience on today's going gives him a solid platform to go one better; the concern is that he has been winless in this recent sequence and may find the 168 lb he shoulders a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Socks Off
runners_data.note: Carries a 220-day absence into this and is a redistributed prominent type shown on the lead only because no confirmed front-runner exists — racing well out of role with a STYLE_FIT of 0.80; the long break is a significant risk flag at Sedgefield on good ground.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has been third three times in recent starts, and our rating of 105 puts him right in contention, but 166 lb is a hefty burden and 220 days off the track is the key concern for a gelding yet to win in this recent spell.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type for Donald McCain (0/6 in 14 days), wearing a tongue-tie; consistent placer at 2m-2m2f on good ground but has yet to demonstrate the stamina for 2m4f convincingly, and the trainer's current cold spell is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has finished third on three occasions in recent starts, American Empire has run over today's going and arrives here on a competitive weight of 166 lb, with our rating of 99 marking him a leading danger; the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five outings.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Excellent good-going record (15/15 runs on similar ground) and twice a winner at 2m4f+; naturally a hold-up horse, shifted forward on the map simply because so many rear-runners crowd the back — his class and distance form remain the standout credentials in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but did finish second three runs back and third four runs back, giving Indian Sunbird some each-way claims; he has run over today's trip and going, though 165 lb is a stiff ask and a 37-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: William Yeats
runners_data.note: A five-year-old lightly raced on good ground (only 2/6 runs on similar going) and returning from 140 days off; wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up type shown in midfield by necessity rather than preference — the layoff and good-going uncertainty are real discounts.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat of late with back-to-back thirds in his last two starts, and a winner five starts back, William Yeats has experience over today's trip and going; the 140-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 113 marks him as the clear class act here.

runners_data.name: Lipstick Traces
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse at 2m4f-2m6f on good ground, but has not won in five attempts and carries a fall (F) in recent form; a true hold-up runner mapped forward because the rear is oversubscribed, and the absence of a win at any trip tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lipstick Traces does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a 44-day freshen-up may help, though she shoulders 164 lb as a mare rated 92 officially.

runners_data.name: Pepite De Saphir
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Rebecca Menzies, wearing a tongue-tie and returning from 85 days; has placed at 2m4f but has a pulled-up run to explain and no wins in current going conditions — moved into midfield position purely by field-crowding logic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pepite De Saphir does show a second three starts back to suggest she retains ability, though a pulled-up run two starts back and 85 days off the track are questions she must answer under a hefty 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: Held up naturally, shown in midfield as a consequence of the overcrowded rear; wears a hood (previously ran in p headgear), five-year-old for David Thompson who is 0/4 in 14 days — placed at 2m4f on good but form figures suggest inconsistency at a short price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Top Flight Century faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: Two wins at 2m2f-2m4f on good ground and consistent recent form (-51316) make this one of the more bankable form entries; a hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity, but trainer Barry John Murphy is 0/3 in 14 days and the 40-day layoff is modest rather than alarming.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 157 lb, Makinbecon is hard to fancy on his latest sixth, though he has winning form in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes is a powerful Sedgefield booking for Micky Hammond (trainer in form: 2/4 in 14 days); a hold-up runner carried to midfield by field logic, but OR 79 is the lowest in the race and recent form (42FP5-) includes a fall and a pulled-up — class drop alone does not resolve the form concerns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Lillistar has a tough task carrying 151 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and the 24-day break at least means she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Socks Off is the only confirmed pace-setter in this field, though the data flags this horse as a redistributed prominent type racing out of natural role — in reality, the pace will be modest and unlikely to be pressured with any authority, creating a steady, galloping tempo over 2m4f on good ground at Sedgefield. With Socks Off setting a sustainable, uncontested lead, the race will unfold in a strung-out fashion with the pack tracking in behind, setting up a thorough stamina test rather than a sprint finish. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Indian Sunbird, William Yeats, Lipstick Traces, Pepite De Saphir, Top Flight Century, Makinbecon, and Lillistar are all natural rear-runners redistributed into midfield positions because the race simply cannot accommodate them all at the back. Given the lone, unhurried pace source and a field of closers who will be unable to operate from their natural positions, this race shape strongly favours horses with genuine class from behind who can travel smoothly in a convoy and produce a sustained galloping finish — patient, versatile hold-up horses with good form on good going and 2m4f+ experience hold the structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pace, Closers Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Socks Off sets a steady tempo unchallenged and the hold-up pack tracks in a tight convoy before a grinding, stamina-led finish.
scenarios.body: Socks Off controls the race at a sustainable clip, but the long 2m4f trip on good ground means the closers who travel smoothly in midfield will pick their moment jumping the final flights and grind out the finish; Indian Sunbird and Makinbecon, both proven over this trip in good going, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Socks Off, operating on a long layoff but getting a completely uncontested lead, conserves enough energy to pinch a lead that the hold-up pack cannot quite close.
scenarios.body: With no genuine rival to force the pace up, Socks Off dictates every yard and the convoy of hold-up types — racing out of role — leaves too much to do at the final hurdle; the horse benefits from the soft lead and clear jumping visibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield types — particularly Indian Sunbird or William Yeats — secures a forward berth and dictates from the front rank.
scenarios.body: Racing nearer the pace than their natural style, a horse with the class and hurdle jumping technique to travel prominently gets first run jumping the last; Indian Sunbird's strong good-going record over 2m4f makes this the likeliest version of the scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the convoy bunches and a true deep closer threads through late to snatch a messy finish.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine chaos — fallers, interference or a sudden collapse of tempo — for a hold-up horse to make ground from further back than the map shows; Aimeric and American Empire, both capable of finishing powerfully, are the most likely beneficiaries if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Indian Sunbird's good-going profile is unmatched in this field (15/15 on similar ground) — watch whether James Best can manoeuvre from a midfield position he would not naturally choose, as any trouble in running could cost him the race.

Makinbecon has won twice at this trip on good ground and carries strong recent form; watch the 40-day break against Callum Pritchard getting a clear run from what will be a congested midfield, as a clean journey suits this horse most.

Socks Off's 220-day absence is a major stamina-and-fitness unknown — watch for signs of laboured jumping or fading from the third-last, which could trigger a chaotic finish if the lone pace source collapses.

The pack of redistributed hold-up types mapped into midfield creates a real risk of a bunched, traffic-heavy race — watch for Lipstick Traces (recent fall in form) and Top Flight Century causing interference at the hurdles on a tightly grouped turn at Sedgefield.

William Yeats's 140-day layoff combined with limited good-ground experience means Jonathan England may ride conservatively early; watch whether the horse travels fluently, as any laboured movement in the first mile will signal he is not ready to fire off this break.

races.name: Bodhi Creative Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: You Be Lucky Jean
runners_data.comment: Sole recent start ended in victory, and she has run over today's trip and going, giving her a fitness edge to weigh against 96 days off; at the head of our ratings, You Be Lucky Jean looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Youlooklikeyourmum
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Youlooklikeyourmum makes her debut carrying 156 lb and represents a complete unknown with every improvement still ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Arc Kunoichi
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Arc Kunoichi makes her debut carrying 153 lb, with nothing in the book yet but plenty unknown and potentially untapped.

runners_data.name: Cumnock
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Cumnock steps into the unknown here carrying 153 lb, but with no form to weigh up she remains a fascinating unknown quantity and could be anything.

runners_data.name: Grey Day
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Grey Day arrives with her record a blank slate and plenty of scope for improvement; carrying 153 lb, she is one to watch as connections look to get her off the mark.

runners_data.name: Megatothemax
runners_data.comment: Megatothemax shaped with real promise on her most recent start, finishing third, and has experience over today's trip to call on; rated 102 and ranked second in the field, she looks a leading danger, though the 86-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Reverse Charge
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Reverse Charge is a filly yet to score who arrives at the track as a fascinating unknown; carrying 153 lb, she merits close inspection as connections unveil her for the first time.

runners_data.name: Tottie's Moon
runners_data.comment: Tottie's Moon has run over today's trip and going and, rated 92 in a field of nine, she shapes as a leading contender on form profile, though her fifth last time out and a lengthy 78-day break are the main questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: True Measure
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, True Measure returns from a 177-day absence carrying 153 lb, and though yet to win in recent starts, her light campaign leaves plenty of scope for better.
